answers.2: Red and Blue — task-oriented profiles that complement each other: drive/decisions plus analysis/quality (though friction is possible); socially, Green and Blue also pair well as calm, steady types

answers.4: Blue — precise, meticulous, follows procedures, low error tolerance
answers.5: Yellow — loves attention, being center stage, enthusiastic communicator
answers.6: Blue — organized, structured, keeps meticulous records
answers.7: Blue — needs data, facts and analysis before deciding
answers.8: Blue — punctual, disciplined, respects schedules (Green is also reliable, but Blue is the strictest about time)
answers.9: Red — pragmatic, results over rules, breaks procedures to get things done
answers.10: Yellow — open, experimental, likes novelty and improvisation
answers.11: Green — takes criticism personally and holds onto emotional wounds longest
answers.12: Yellow — disorganized but has a great network and knows who to contact
answers.13: Red — decisive, wants to be in control of decisions
answers.14: Yellow — expressive, wants to stand out and impress
answers.15: Red — thrives on challenges, competition and winning
answers.16: Red — quick, decisive, judges others fast and bluntly
answers.17: All four together (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) — a complementary team with a driver, communicator, supporter and analyst; no single 'best' pairing
answers.19: Yellow — enthusiastic, quickly embraces new ideas; Red also adopts fast if it serves results, but Yellow is quickest to get excited
answers.20: Red — delegates but doesn't trust others to do it right, so takes it back over
answers.22: Blue — follows instructions precisely to the last step
answers.23: No single answer — depends on the individual's actual social circle; statistically Greens are often cited as the most common profile in the general population, but I can't know my 'social circle'
